citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Expressing consensus on appointment of Muslim Guiamaden as Wali of the Bangsamoro.
citizen_summary.is_it_binding: Resolutions express Parliament's official position or direct BARMM offices; unlike Autonomy Acts they generally do not create binding law for the public, but internal-rules resolutions bind the Parliament itself.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: Res. 445 (2024): Expressing consensus on appointment of Muslim Guiamaden as Wali of the Bangsamoro. Touches Islamic institutional life - Shari'ah courts, qur'anic achievement, religious observance, fatwa implementation. For Muslim residents these resolutions push the infrastructure of faith: more Shari'ah judges, recognized scholars, supported observances.

for_specific_groups.Muslim residents: Better access to Shari'ah justice and religious services
for_specific_groups.Ulama & students: Recognition and career pathways (bar, bench, kulliyah)

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: All of BARMM unless the title names a specific place
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Immediately as an official position; concrete action depends on the addressed agency
what_you_can_do: If the resolution urges an agency to act, cite it when following up with that agency
Share it - resolutions gain force through public attention
Ask your MP to follow through with legislation if the issue needs a binding law

key_terms_explained.Adopted resolution: An official position or instruction of the Parliament - persuasive and political, but not a law binding the public.
key_terms_explained.BAA: Bangsamoro Autonomy Act - a regional law passed by the Bangsamoro Parliament, applying inside BARMM alongside national laws.

benefits.headline: Stronger infrastructure of faith and Shari'ah justice.

direct_benefits.benefit: Pushes for more Shari'ah courts/judges = faster access to Islamic personal-law justice
direct_benefits.how_to_access: File in Shari'ah courts; cite the backlog resolutions when courts are vacant

indirect_benefits: Recognition and pathways for ulama and qur'anic achievers
limitations: Court creation/appointments rest with the Supreme Court and national bodies
